_note: Key counties per state: why each one matters and what to look for. Numbers (2024 margin, share of the state vote, break-even benchmark) are computed from data in the workbook; this file holds only the judgment calls. Edit freely.
GA: Fulton
Largest vote bank for Democrats (Atlanta).
Raw D vote margin matters more than the percentage. If turnout lags 2022, Democrats need bigger margins elsewhere.
Gwinnett
Most diverse big county in the state; swung slightly R from 2020 to 2024 as Hispanic and Asian voters moved.
Whether the 2024 drift toward R continues or snaps back. Best single read on nonwhite swing voters.
Cobb
College-educated suburbs that flipped D in 2016 and kept moving left.
A margin above 2024 means the suburban realignment is still paying Democrats.
DeKalb
Heavily Black, highly educated D base.
Turnout versus 2022. Its margin barely moves, so the vote count is the signal.
Henry
Fast-growing Black suburb south of Atlanta, and the biggest D gain of any large Georgia county from 2020 to 2024 (about 9 points).
Whether that gain holds in a midterm with lower Black turnout.
Clayton
Most Democratic county in Georgia, majority Black.
Turnout. Its margin barely moves, so the raw vote count is what matters.
Forsyth
Wealthy, college-educated exurb that's still strongly R.
Any shrinking of the R margin here signals college-educated Republicans defecting.
Chatham
Savannah. A mid-size D county with a large Black population.
A non-Atlanta check on Black turnout and margin.
Cherokee
Georgia's biggest Republican vote bank: a fast-growing exurb north of Atlanta that gave Trump about 63,000 net votes in 2024.
Republican turnout. Its margin barely moves (R+40 in 2020, 2022 and 2024), so a turnout index under 100 here is the clearest sign of a Republican enthusiasm gap.
Hall
Gainesville. The third-biggest R net-vote county, and nearly 30% Hispanic.
Margin and turnout both. An R margin well under R+44 points to Hispanic voters moving back toward Democrats; turnout under the state pace means the exurban base isn't showing up.
Bartow
Northwest Georgia exurb along I-75 at R+51, a stand-in for the small-town Republican base.
Turnout. The margin is locked in (R+51 in 2020, 2022 and 2024), so the vote count is the signal.
NC: Wake
Largest county (Raleigh), with fast-growing college-educated suburbs.
Turnout growth plus margin. Wake has been adding thousands of net D votes every cycle.
Mecklenburg
Charlotte. Second-biggest D vote bank, with a large Black population.
Its margin slipped 2.2 points toward R in 2024. A rebound is a good D sign.
Durham
Deep-blue Research Triangle county.
Turnout. The margin is near its ceiling.
Guilford
Greensboro. A big, racially mixed county that tracks the statewide trend.
Margin compared with its 2022 and 2024 baselines.
New Hanover
Wilmington. A true swing county, almost exactly tied in 2024.
Whichever side wins it by a few points is usually having a good night statewide.
Buncombe
Asheville. Hurricane Helene hit it in 2024, and it still swung D.
Turnout recovery after Helene, and whether the 2024 D gain holds.
Johnston
Booming exurb southeast of Raleigh, still strongly R but trending D.
R margin under about 20 means Democrats are making suburban growth work for them.
Robeson
Lumbee Native American, Black and white rural county that swung hard R (about 9 points in 2024).
Bellwether for rural working-class nonwhite voters. A Cooper bounce-back here is a strong D signal.
Union
Charlotte's fast-growing southeastern exurb, about 35,000 net R votes in 2024.
Suburban Republicans. College-educated growth has kept it flat (R+24.5 in 2020, R+25.5 in 2024). Well under that, with turnout on pace, means suburban Republicans are slipping.
Randolph
The most Republican county in North Carolina with 100,000+ people (R+58), in the Piedmont between Greensboro and Charlotte.
Turnout. The margin is near its ceiling, so whether small-town Republicans turn out in a midterm is the question.
Davidson
The state's biggest R net-vote county (about 44,000 in 2024), working-class Piedmont.
Turnout and margin together: R+48 at a turnout index of 100 or better means the Republican base is fully there.
MI: Wayne
Detroit and its inner suburbs. The biggest D vote bank, which collapsed 8.6 points toward R in 2024 (including Dearborn's Arab American vote).
Detroit turnout and Dearborn-area margins. A rebound toward 2022's +44 is the clearest D path.
Oakland
Large, educated suburban county that anchors D statewide wins.
Margin. It was D+23 in 2022 (Whitmer) but only D+11 for Harris.
Macomb
Classic blue-collar bellwether that went R+14 in 2024.
Whether Democrats get it back toward even, as Whitmer did in 2022 (D+5).
Kent
Grand Rapids. West Michigan swing county, D since 2020.
College-educated and religious voters. A margin above +10 is very good for D.
Washtenaw
Ann Arbor. Students and university staff.
Turnout, especially campus precincts. Midterm youth turnout drops are the risk.
Genesee
Flint. A union-heavy county where the D margin has been eroding.
Working-class Black and white voters. A margin near 2022's +19 is a strong D sign.
Saginaw
Long-running bellwether that has gone with the statewide winner in most recent races.
Whoever wins it likely wins the state.
Ottawa
Deep-red, religious, increasingly college-educated West Michigan suburb.
The R margin shrinking below 20 means GOP erosion with educated conservatives.
Livingston
Affluent, college-educated exurb between Detroit and Lansing: R+24 in 2024 but only R+13 in the 2022 governor race.
Whether Republicans hold their presidential margin in a midterm. Closer to 2022's R+13 than 2024's R+24 means suburban Republicans are defecting or staying home.
St. Clair
Blue-collar Thumb county (Port Huron) that moved 4.4 pts toward R from 2020 to 2024.
Working-class Republican turnout. Its 2022 margin (R+17) was half its 2024 margin, so a midterm drop-off among these voters shows up here first.
OH: Franklin
Columbus. The largest and fastest-growing D county.
Turnout and margin. Brown needs big numbers here to offset rural Ohio.
Cuyahoga
Cleveland. Historic D base with declining population.
Turnout. Weak Cleveland turnout sank Democrats in 2022.
Hamilton
Cincinnati. Formerly R, now reliably D because of suburban college voters.
Margin compared with 2024's +15.
Summit
Akron. A union-heavy swing-ish county.
A D margin of +10 or more is needed to run competitively statewide.
Montgomery
Dayton. Roughly even in 2024, about 11 points left of the state.
Democrats need to win it clearly to be competitive statewide.
Mahoning
Youngstown. Former D stronghold that swung 7.6 points R in 2024.
Blue-collar ancestral Democrats. Brown's comeback depends on voters like these.
Lorain
Blue-collar county west of Cleveland that went narrowly R in 2020 and further R in 2024.
Whether working-class white voters return to Brown.
Delaware
Wealthy, college-educated Columbus exurb, still R.
A shrinking R margin shows suburban defections.
Butler
Cincinnati's northern suburbs and Ohio's biggest R net-vote county (about 48,000 in 2024).
An R margin at R+26 or better with turnout on pace means Republicans are fine. Back near its 2022 level (R+24) or lower is a warning for them.
Warren
College-educated exurb between Cincinnati and Dayton, R+32 and barely moved from 2020 to 2024.
College-educated Republicans. Any real slippage here suggests the Democrat is winning crossover votes.
Stark
Canton. A classic working-class bellwether that went from R+19 in 2020 to R+22 in 2024.
Whether working-class voters come back to Democrats. Near its 2022 level (R+16) is a good D sign; R+22 or worse means the 2024 coalition held.
TX: Harris
Houston. The largest county, and it swung 7.8 points R in 2024.
Margin. Above +10 means Democrats regained ground with Hispanic and Black voters.
Dallas
Big D base that swung 9.6 points R in 2024.
Margin recovery toward 2020's +32.
Tarrant
Fort Worth. The classic Texas swing county: Beto narrowly won it in 2018 and Biden barely won it in 2020, then it went R+5 in 2024.
If Democrats win Tarrant, they're likely within striking distance statewide.
Bexar
San Antonio. Majority Hispanic, D, swung R in 2024.
Hispanic swing in an urban setting.
Travis
Austin. Very high D turnout and margin.
Turnout. Democrats need it to keep growing.
Collin
Rich, college-educated Dallas suburb, R+11 in 2024.
Suburban shift. Talarico needs it close to single digits.
Fort Bend
One of the most diverse counties in America (Houston suburbs). Nearly flipped R in 2024.
Asian, Black and Hispanic suburban voters.
Hidalgo
Rio Grande Valley. Swung 20 points R from 2020 to 2024.
The headline Hispanic-realignment test. Any D rebound here is huge news.
Montgomery
Houston's northern exurb and the biggest Republican vote bank in Texas (about 140,000 net R votes in 2024).
Republican turnout. Republicans offset Harris, Dallas and Travis with exurban turnout; an index under 100 here is a red flag for them.
Lubbock
West Texas hub, 37% Hispanic, that moved 7 pts toward R from 2020 to 2024.
Whether the 2024 Hispanic shift toward R holds. A margin back toward 2020 (R+33) is good for Democrats.
Comal
Fast-growing Hill Country exurb between San Antonio and Austin, college-educated and R+46.
Turnout. It's adding voters every cycle, so it should take a bigger share of the state vote; if it doesn't, Republican turnout is soft.
IA: Polk
Des Moines. The D vote bank, about 15% of the state's vote.
Margin and turnout. Democrats need it well above 2024's +11.
Linn
Cedar Rapids. A union county that's been sliding toward R.
A D margin near +15 is a good sign.
Johnson
Iowa City. University of Iowa, very D.
Student turnout.
Dallas
Fast-growing, college-educated Des Moines suburb, still R.
Suburban defections. Flipping it would be a big D night.
Scott
Davenport. Former D county that went R in 2024.
Classic Mississippi River swing county.
Black Hawk
Waterloo. Union and Black voters, almost tied in 2024.
Working-class D strength.
Dubuque
Catholic working-class river county that went from D to R.
Ancestral Democrats returning or not.
Sioux
Iowa's most Republican county (R+72), the core of northwest Iowa's Republican base.
Turnout. The margin is maxed out, so the R vote count is the signal.
Woodbury
Sioux City, 20% Hispanic; moved 7.5 pts toward R from 2020 to 2024.
Hispanic and working-class voters. A margin back toward 2020 (R+16) is good for Democrats.
Pottawattamie
Council Bluffs, Iowa's side of metro Omaha: working-class and R+20.
Working-class swing: R+17 in 2020, R+20 in 2024. Its turnout also tests whether the Republican base outside the big metros is showing up.
ME: Cumberland
Portland. A quarter of the state's vote and very D.
Margin and turnout. Collins has historically cut into it.
York
Southern Maine. Bigger and more swingy than Cumberland.
Collins's crossover strength. Democrats want about +15.
Kennebec
Augusta. Roughly even, about 10 points right of the state in 2024.
A Jackson win here would point to a comfortable statewide win.
Penobscot
Bangor. The 2nd District's population center, leans R.
Jackson is from northern Maine. Watch whether he cuts into the R margin here.
Androscoggin
Lewiston-Auburn. A blue-collar former D county that now leans R.
Working-class swing.
Aroostook
The County. Rural far north, where Jackson is from.
A home-region bounce for Jackson would show up here first.
Somerset
Rural central Maine (Skowhegan), R+28 and among the three biggest R net-vote counties.
Rural Republican turnout in the 2nd District. It moved 3.5 pts toward R from 2020 to 2024 but was only R+19 in the 2022 governor race.
NH: Manchester and Nashua. The biggest county, and it votes close to the state.
Margin. Whoever wins it big usually wins NH.
Seacoast and Boston-commuter suburbs. Lean R, and the GOP's biggest vote source.
Sununu-name strength. A big R margin here is the GOP path.
Dover and UNH. A D-leaning college county.
The North Country: rural and working-class, and the biggest 2020-to-2024 shift toward R in the state (about 8 pts).
Whether that shift holds in a midterm: it was only R+3 in 2022 versus R+14 in 2024.
MN: Minneapolis. The giant D vote bank, about 22% of the state.
Turnout. Its margin is near the ceiling.
Southern Twin Cities suburbs, D-leaning swing.
Margin above +13 (2024) is good for Flanagan.
Tafoya needs a clear win here.
Rochester (Mayo Clinic). Educated, D-leaning, a few points left of the state.
Duluth and the Iron Range. Historic DFL labor country, eroding.
Range towns moving R would be bad news for Flanagan.
St. Cloud. Strongly R central Minnesota.
Fast-growing exurb northwest of the Twin Cities and Minnesota's biggest R net-vote county (about 26,000 in 2024).
Exurban Republican turnout. An index under 100 here plus strong Hennepin turnout is a bad night for Republicans.
Exurban corridor northwest of the Twin Cities, R+35.
Margin and turnout. It moved 2 pts toward R from 2020 to 2024; a reversal is an early D sign.
KS: Kansas City suburbs. A quarter of the state's vote, college-educated, trending D.
A big D margin here is required for any upset.
If Democrats get within single digits, they're competitive statewide.
Democrats need to win it clearly for an upset.
Kansas City, Kansas. Black and Hispanic D base that swung R in 2024.
Manhattan (K-State, Fort Riley). Swingy college town.
Wichita's eastern exurb and the biggest R net-vote county after Sedgwick.
Turnout plus a margin near R+42. A softer margin means suburban Wichita Republicans are drifting.
Hutchinson. A small-city county that stands in for central Kansas.
Midterm turnout leans R here: R+45 in the 2022 Senate race vs R+35 in 2024. Republicans want it closer to 2022.
NE: Osborn needs a big win in Omaha on top of rural crossover.
Close to even here would be a great Osborn sign.
Grand Island. A third Hispanic, meatpacking.
Osborn's working-class pitch and Hispanic voters.
Osborn's 2024 strategy was cutting rural R margins. Watch whether he does it again.
North Platte. Rural western Nebraska, railroad and union history.
SC: College-educated coastal county. D in 2024, but 7 points less so than in 2020.
Suburban shift. Democrats need a clear win.
Columbia. Large Black population, D base.
The Upstate's largest county, strongly R but educated.
R margin shrinking means suburban defections.
Myrtle Beach. Fast-growing retiree R stronghold.
Hilton Head. Wealthy retirees, and a growing Black and military population.
Upstate. Moved 6 pts toward R from 2020 to 2024, about 52,000 net R votes.
Upstate Republican turnout. The Upstate is where Republicans bank their statewide margin.
Columbia's suburbs, about 49,000 net R votes and nearly 6% of the state's vote.
Suburban Republicans. It was R+42 in the 2022 Senate race; Republicans want something close to that, not 2024's R+34.
MS: Jackson. Majority Black, the D base.
Black turnout. Democrats need it high everywhere in the Delta too.
The R margin shrinking is a long-term D trend.
Gulfport and Biloxi. The Gulf Coast.
FL: Miami-Dade
Majority Hispanic and the biggest county. It swung about 19 points R from 2020 to 2024 and voted R for president for the first time since 1988.
The best early test of whether 2024's Hispanic shift toward R holds or snaps back. Read it alongside Hidalgo (TX) and Osceola.
Broward
Florida's largest D vote bank, with a large Black and Caribbean population.
Margin recovery toward 2020's D+30, and turnout.
Palm Beach
Wealthy, mixed, and roughly even in 2024.
Suburban and retiree swing.
Hillsborough
Tampa. A swing county that went R in 2024.
Its margin compared with 2024's R+3 is a clean read of the suburban environment.
Pinellas
St. Petersburg. An old bellwether that has moved R.
Same read as Hillsborough, with older voters.
Orange
Orlando. A large Puerto Rican and Hispanic population, solidly D.
Non-Cuban Hispanic swing. Pair it with Osceola.
Osceola
Majority Hispanic (mostly Puerto Rican). Flipped R in 2024.
Whether Puerto Rican voters swing back.
Duval
Jacksonville. About 29% Black, flips back and forth.
Black turnout plus suburban swing in one county.
Lee
Fort Myers. The biggest R vote bank outside Miami-Dade (about 111,000 net R votes), and it moved 9 pts toward R from 2020 to 2024.
Retiree and exurban Republican turnout. Republicans need it at R+29 or better on full turnout.
Polk
Lakeland, on the I-4 corridor; 30% Hispanic and moved 6 pts toward R from 2020 to 2024.
Puerto Rican and other Hispanic voters on I-4. A margin back toward 2020 (R+15) is a good D sign.
Pasco
Tampa's northern exurb, about 80,000 net R votes.
Republican turnout. If Pasco's share of the vote lags, the Tampa-area R base isn't showing up.
VA: Fairfax
Northern Virginia's giant: highly educated, many federal workers, D+36.
Margin compared with 2024's D+36. Home to many federal workers, so it's a read on how they're voting.
Loudoun
Fast-growing, college-educated exurb that swung R in 2024.
Read it with Collin (TX), Forsyth (GA) and Delaware (OH).
Prince William
Diverse suburb, with large Hispanic and Black populations.
Suburban swing among voters of color.
Virginia Beach
Military-heavy swing city, D+3 in 2024.
A bellwether for the Kiggans-Luria House race (VA-02) too.
Chesterfield
Richmond suburb that has trended D.
College suburbs outside Northern Virginia.
Henrico
Richmond suburb, about 30% Black and educated.
Black and suburban turnout.
Richmond city
The D base in central Virginia.
Turnout.
Hanover
Richmond's college-educated Republican suburb, the R counterpart to Henrico and Chesterfield.
College-educated Republicans. It moved 1.3 pts toward D from 2020 to 2024; more of that is a national suburban signal.
Bedford
Lynchburg-area Republican base at R+51, the biggest R net-vote county in Virginia.
Rural Republican turnout. The margin is locked in, so the vote count is the signal.
KY: Louisville. Kentucky's D base, where Booker is from.
Booker's home margin and Black turnout.
Lexington. A college town that's solidly D.
Northern Kentucky suburbs of Cincinnati, R+22.
Suburban swing in the earliest-closing state.
Eastern Kentucky coal country, where polls close at 6 PM ET. Among the first counties in the nation to report.
Ancestral Democrats. Booker ran far ahead of Harris in eastern Kentucky in 2022, so compare against both 2024 and 2022.
Eastern Kentucky, R+60 in 2024 but only R+31 for Senate in 2022.
